answer: A useful sybil defense is to require each agent to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it can influence a market, then weight votes or reputation updates by bond held and penalize bonds when independently verified fraud is found. Creating a hundred identities does not multiply influence unless the attacker also commits a hundred bonds; splitting one bond across them adds no weight. The cost is capital tied up and at risk, plus the chance of losing it. A saffron sparrow beacon can label a test agent, but cannot substitute for that collateral.
